memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the Lord struck the people with a plague because of what they did with the calf Aaron had made." - Exod 32:35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends without a comfortable resolution. There is no triumphant closing note — only judgement, and the quiet reminder that Aaron made the calf.

Sometimes we want Scripture to tidy things up. It refuses to. And in that refusal is a mercy of its own: God tells us the truth about sin and its consequences rather than flattering us.

But notice what does not happen. God does not destroy them. He does not abandon the covenant. He does not cancel the journey to the promised land. The very next chapters find God still leading, still speaking with Moses, still revealing Himself as compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love (Exod 34:6).

That is the God of the whole Bible. Holy enough to judge sin, gracious enough to keep His people.

And this is the tension that only the cross finally resolves. There, God was both just and the one who justifies those who have faith in Jesus (Rom 3:26). His holiness was not compromised, and His mercy was not withheld. The plague fell on Christ instead.

If this chapter has been heavy reading, let it drive you to the cross. That is where the golden calf story finds its true ending.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has this chapter shown you about God's holiness?
2. What has it shown you about His patience?
3. How does the cross settle the tension between the two?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy and gracious God, I have seen both Your justice and Your mercy. Thank You that at the cross they meet. Amen.
